name: 1-cay-ma
prompt:
SCENE: transplanting rice seedlings. ME bends over in a flooded paddy, ankle-deep in water, pushing a small bunch of young green rice seedlings into the mud; neat rows of seedlings stretch away behind her, reflections in the water. BA carries a bundle of seedlings on the bank. Early morning light.

RECURRING FAMILY (draw them consistently): BA (the father): Vietnamese farmer about 58, short salt-and-pepper hair with grey temples, kind tanned face, light green work shirt with rolled sleeves, brown trousers. ME (the mother): about 55, round kind face, straight black shoulder-length hair with thin bangs, Vietnamese non la conical palm-leaf hat, brown peasant blouse (ao nau). ANH HAI (their son): about 28, short black hair, plain light shirt, brown trousers.

STYLE: semi-realistic Chinese manhua illustration in a wuxia comic style, applied to a peaceful Vietnamese countryside scene. Rough, strong black-brown ink linework with dry-brush strokes, detailed faces and cloth folds, high-contrast cel shadows, cinematic lighting. The background is a traditional ink-wash (thuy mac) painting: soft grey and warm washes, misty distance, fading to off-white paper (#FBF7EE) at the edges, with a little loose ink splatter. Warm limited palette: earth browns (#4A2C1A, #8B5A2B), golden rice (#D9A13B), straw (#F2E2B6), skin tones, a little young-rice green (#6E8B3D) and soft sky blue only in the sky. No armour, no weapons, no fantasy.

Setting: the countryside of Hai Duong, northern Vietnam, a family that grows yellow-flower sticky rice (nep cai hoa vang). Wide 16:9 composition. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no signature, no seal stamp.
